name: Restaurant or cafe
description: Restaurants, cafes, tea houses, bakeries and food outlets. People decide with their eyes and their phones: the menu, the photographs, the opening hours and one tap to order or reserve.

goals.prompt: What should the website do for your food business? Name the one or two results that matter most.
goals.why: A food site is judged by orders placed, tables booked and people walking in, not by visits.

recommendation.statement: Get customers to order ahead or reserve a table
Bring people in with the menu, the photographs and the place
recommendation.metric: visits from Google Maps and the site

goals.reason: The two results every food business wants.

audience.prompt: Who comes to you, and what do they want from a visit or an order? One per line; add if known: wants: ... | proof: ... | action: ... | from: ... | mood: ...
audience.why: Students, office workers, families and tourists want different things at different hours.

recommendation.need: See the menu, check the hours, and order or reserve quickly

recommendation.segment: New visitors who found you on Google or Instagram
recommendation.need: Judge the food and the place from photographs, then find the way in

audience.reason: The two groups every food site serves; research in P2 refines them.

heroMustHave: A real photograph of the food or the room that makes someone hungry, not a stock image
Today's opening hours and the area or landmark, so a visitor knows it is open and near

pages.title: Home
pages.purpose: Make the food and the place irresistible, show today's hours and lead to ordering or booking

pages.title: Menu
pages.purpose: Show the full menu with prices, dietary tags and the bestsellers first

pages.title: Order
pages.purpose: Take an order for pickup or delivery in a few taps

pages.title: Gallery
pages.purpose: Show the dishes, the room and the people with real photographs

pages.title: Visit
pages.purpose: Give the address, hours, map, parking and how to reach the place

pages.title: Our Story
pages.purpose: Tell why the place exists and what makes the food different

pages.title: Reservations
pages.purpose: Let groups book a table with the date, time and party size

pages.title: Events and Catering
pages.purpose: Sell private dining, birthdays, corporate orders and catering with packages and an enquiry form

pages.title: Offers and Loyalty
pages.purpose: Show current offers, combos and the loyalty programme

pages.title: Reviews
pages.purpose: Let customers speak with their ratings and photographs

pages.title: Questions
pages.purpose: Answer delivery area, dietary needs, parking, payment and booking questions

pages.title: Franchise
pages.purpose: Show the model, the investment and the support for people who want to open an outlet

pages.title: From the Kitchen
pages.purpose: Share recipes, seasonal specials and stories that bring people back

pages.title: Careers
pages.purpose: Recruit cooks, baristas and front-of-house with the roles and a way to apply

forms.purpose: Plan an event or catering order

questions.prompt: How do customers get your food?
questions.why: Ordering, delivery and dine-in each need different buttons and different copy.
questions.reason: The minimum every food outlet offers.

questions.prompt: How should an online order reach you?
questions.why: An order form that nobody sees is worse than none. This decides what the Order button does.

options.label: A form on the site that comes to us
Link out to Zomato or Swiggy

questions.reason: The fastest option for a small kitchen to handle.

questions.prompt: What do you have for the menu?
questions.why: Typing a menu from photographs takes care; a spreadsheet is fastest.

options.label: A spreadsheet or document with items and prices

questions.prompt: What are your opening hours, and do they change on weekends or holidays?
questions.why: Hours are shown in the hero and on the visit page, so a wrong time is an angry customer.

questions.prompt: Which three dishes or drinks should a first-time visitor try?
questions.why: The hero and the menu lead with these.

questions.prompt: How would a regular describe the place in three words?
questions.why: It sets the tone of the copy and the design.

questions.prompt: Do you host events, private dining or take large orders?
questions.why: If yes, the Events and Catering page and its form are built.

questions.prompt: Which social or review pages should the site link to?
questions.why: Instagram and Google reviews are often the real proof.

/: hero with a real food or room photograph, today's hours, the primary action and the menu link
bestsellers or signature items with photographs
how to order: dine-in, pickup, delivery
the place: address, map and hours
a closing order or booking call to action
/menu: categories with items, prices and dietary tags
an order button that stays in view on a phone
/visit: how to get there and where to park
a call and a directions button

compliance: Prices, opening hours and addresses must be exactly what the client supplied; a wrong price or hour is a customer complaint
Never claim dietary properties (vegan, gluten-free, halal) the client has not confirmed
Sample items and prices must be marked as samples until the client confirms them

extras.note: A short loop of steam, pouring or the kitchen makes people hungry; it must be silent and fall back to a photograph.
One signature object (a cup, a pizza box, a kulhad) can add delight as a small interactive section, but never in front of the order button.
Real photographs of the food and the room are what decide a visit.
A map and a directions button answer the question every new visitor has.
